walkthroughs.body_html:
Materials — a core area of GCSE Chemistry.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Materials brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Materials.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

Why does water have a bent shape rather than linear?
options: Oxygen has two bonding pairs and two lone pairs, giving a tetrahedral electron geometry but a bent molecular shape.
Water is bent because oxygen is heavier than hydrogen and weighs the middle down.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Water is bent because the hydrogens repel each other and push apart.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.

mcqs.q: How does a buffer maintain its pH when small amounts of acid are added?
options: A buffer destroys added acid by changing it into water vapour.
A buffer prevents any H+ ions from being added to the solution at all.
The conjugate base in the buffer reacts with added H+ to remove it, keeping pH nearly constant.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
